Area.evidence_source: Men may be unable to articulate emotion because they don't know how or believe that expressing emotion is not permissible for men. At the same time, men are in a dilemma of not being taken seriously if expressing their distress is considered "too behavioral" or "with inappropriate affect." This dilemma creates serious communication difficulties for patients and providers.Many life experiences led men in the study to have negative expectations of health care providers, and perhaps to feel that no help is available to them. Many struggle with a realization that they need help but fear that in seeking help they may have control taken away from them. These struggles may lead to delays in seeking help, unexpected or unwanted emergency department visits, and inpatient admissions. Our data also indicates that service providers in these settings are perceived to be disinterested about and hostile toward suicidal men with personality and/or substance use disorders, leading to some negative experiences.Anecdotally, many of the men in the study who joined a group intervention expressed hope for the future and some were able to begin more formal treatment program for their substance abuse.
